author: claude
text: For a process, a property K of its runs, a run r and a step h: it is not the case that every run agreeing with r through step h (the same states up to h, the same labels before h) fails to satisfy: if it adheres to K, it has K.

author: claude
text: For a process, a property K of its runs, a run r and a step h: it is not the case that every run agreeing with r through step h (the same states up to h, the same labels before h) fails to satisfy the claim: if it adheres to K, it has K.

author: claude
text: For a process P, a property K of its runs and a run r: K holds of r if and only if both (i) for every length h some run satisfying K agrees with r up to h, and (ii) if (i) holds, then K holds of r.

author: claude
text: For a process P, a property K of its runs and a run r: K holds of r if and only if both (i) for every length h some run satisfying K agrees with r up to h, as far as an observer can see, and (ii) if (i) holds, then K holds of r.

author: claude
text: For a web W and two level histories l and l', if l widens l' in W (it includes l' and exceeds it), then l' does not widen l in W.

author: claude
text: For a web W and two level histories l and l', if l widens l' in W (it includes l' and exceeds it), then, by the nature of widening, l' does not widen l in W.

author: claude
text: Let L be a flow and W a web, let s list at each step the members of C with positive level in W, and suppose L runs down W at every step from T on. Then for any c in C it is not the case that for every N some step t ≥ N has the level of c in W rising after t.

author: claude
text: Let L be a flow and W a web, let s list at each step the members of C with positive level in W, and suppose L runs down W at every step from T on. Then for any c in C it is not the case that for every N some step t ≥ N has the level of c in W rising after t with inflow from the environment.

author: claude
text: For flows L and L', a web W, a relation o, a Boolean marking m and an element g: g lies within the response of L and L' to m if and only if there is an h marked true by m such that every region containing g and closed under coupling from either L or L' in W under o contains h.

author: claude
text: For flows L and L', a web W, a relation o, a Boolean marking m and an element g: g lies within the response of L and L' to m if and only if there is an h marked true by m such that every region containing g and closed under coupling from either L or L', or a third flow, in W under o contains h.

author: claude
text: In a web W, for two level histories l and l' over conditions: if l widens on l' in W (l includes l' and exceeds it), then l does not keep l' (it is not the case that l and l' each include the other).

author: claude
text: In a web W, for two level histories l and l' that a planner sets over conditions: if l widens on l' in W (l includes l' and exceeds it), then l does not keep l' (it is not the case that l and l' each include the other).

author: claude
text: For a family of basic predicates indexed by i, a list of context predicates and a predicate p derivable from the basis and the context: at any state s where every basic predicate holds and every context predicate holds, p holds at s.

author: claude
text: For a family of basic predicates indexed by i, a list of context predicates and a predicate p derivable from the basis and the context: at any state s of the environment where every basic predicate holds and every context predicate holds, p holds at s.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a predicate O on positions and form-step pairs, a position p and a pair e whose form is active and not undermining at its step: under the never-satisfied predicate, for all level histories l and l', l retains l' and does not add over it; the web's valuation with O and everywhere-true significance is significant; with everywhere-false significance it is not.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a predicate O on positions and form-step pairs, a position p and a pair e whose form is active and not undermining anyone at its step: under the never-satisfied predicate, for all level histories l and l', l retains l' and does not add over it; the web's valuation with O and everywhere-true significance is significant; with everywhere-false significance it is not.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a relation o, a form g, a condition c not o-related to g, and a step u: if up to u each condition other than c that g requires has level meeting g's need, then some raise d of c's level keeps g supported up to u, and wherever W supports g, original and raised levels are alike through o for g.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a relation o, a form g, a condition c not o-related to g, and a step u: if up to u each condition other than c that g requires has level meeting g's need, then some raise d of c's level from the environment keeps g supported up to u, and wherever W supports g, original and raised levels are alike through o for g.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a relation o, a form g and a condition c with g o-related to c: raising c's level by a positive amount d leaves the original and raised levels, at any step t, not alike through o for g.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a relation o, a form g and a condition c with g o-related to c: raising c's level by a positive amount d leaves the original and raised levels, at any step t, in truth not alike through o for g.

author: claude
text: In a web W, with a relation o, form g, level histories l and l', step s and a condition c not o-related to g: if l and l' agree at s on each other condition g depends on or is o-related to, and, when g requires c at s, both meet or both miss g's need for c, they are alike through o for g at s.

author: claude
text: In a web W, with a relation o, form g, level histories l and l', step s and a condition c in the environment not o-related to g: if l and l' agree at s on each other condition g depends on or is o-related to, and, when g requires c at s, both meet or both miss g's need for c, they are alike through o for g at s.

author: claude
text: Given a list of conditions, a Boolean part over forms, a coupling map k, the forms present at each step, a Boolean marking r over steps, forms and conditions, and a condition c: if r is false for c at every step and every form outside the part, then c lies on no loop under k with each coupling cut to zero where r is false for its target condition.

author: claude
text: Given a list of conditions, a Boolean part over forms, a coupling map k, the forms present at each step, a Boolean marking r made by a reader over steps, forms and conditions, and a condition c: if r is false for c at every step and every form outside the part, then c lies on no loop under k with each coupling cut to zero where r is false for its target condition.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a step t, forms f and g and a condition c: f arises at t exactly when its activity comes to be (absent at t, present at t+1); f ceases exactly when its activity ceases to be; g's requiring c forms exactly when it comes to be and dissolves exactly when it ceases to be; and the remaining kinds of change correspond likewise.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a step t, forms f and g and a condition c: f arises at t exactly when its activity comes to be (absent at t, present at t+1); f ceases exactly when its activity ceases to be; g's requiring c forms exactly when it comes to be and dissolves exactly when it ceases to be; and, by one law, the remaining kinds of change correspond likewise.

author: claude
text: For a relation R on items, an item f and a region closed under R that contains f: every item g that lies in every R-closed region containing f lies in this region.

author: claude
text: For a relation R on items, an item f and a region closed under R that contains f: every item g that lies in every R-closed region containing f lies in this region, as a matter of truth.

author: claude
text: Let L be a flow, W a web and c a member of C such that every element takes part in c: it depends on c in W or has a positive take or give of c in L. Then for any f and g, every region containing f and closed under L's sharing relation in W contains g.

author: claude
text: Let L be a flow, W a web and c a member of C such that every element takes part in c: it depends on c in W or has a positive take or give of c from the environment in L. Then for any f and g, every region containing f and closed under L's sharing relation in W contains g.

author: claude
text: Let L be a flow, W a web and c a member of C such that every element depends on c in W and exchanges c in L (at some step it is present with a positive take or give of c). Then for any f and g, every region containing f and closed under L's affecting relation in W contains g.

author: claude
text: Let L be a flow, W a web and c a member of C such that every element depends on c in W and exchanges c with its owner in L (at some step it is present with a positive take or give of c). Then for any f and g, every region containing f and closed under L's affecting relation in W contains g.

author: claude
text: For a hexagram s: its two halves glue, meaning there is a single assignment of lines to heights shown by both the lower and the upper half, if and only if at every height the line of the lower half and the line of the upper half are not opposed.

author: claude
text: For a hexagram s: its two halves glue, meaning there is a single assignment of lines to heights, one underlying order, shown by both the lower and the upper half, if and only if at every height the line of the lower half and the line of the upper half are not opposed.

author: claude
text: Suppose (ℓ + 1)d ≤ x₀. The rule that, after step ℓ, reverses the record entry from ℓ + 1 steps earlier depends only on entries at steps s with s + ℓ < t; and for every record whose entries each have components differing by at most d, the amount starting at x₀ under that rule and record stays within (ℓ + 1)d of x₀ at every step.

author: claude
text: Suppose (ℓ + 1)d ≤ x₀. The rule that, after step ℓ, reverses for its operator the record entry from ℓ + 1 steps earlier depends only on entries at steps s with s + ℓ < t; and for every record whose entries each have components differing by at most d, the amount starting at x₀ under that rule and record stays within (ℓ + 1)d of x₀ at every step.

author: claude
text: For a list of items and a whole-number weight w on items: the list's length times the sum over the list of the squares of w equals the square of the list's total weight plus the sum, over all ordered pairs p, q from the list, of the square of the amount by which w at p exceeds w at q.

author: claude
text: For a list of items and a whole-number weight w on items: the list's length times the sum over the list of the squares of w equals the square of the list's total weight plus the sum, over all ordered pairs p, q from the list, of the square of the amount by which w at p exceeds w at q in the natural order.

author: claude
text: Let G be a list of maps on natural numbers, none of which lowers its argument (x ≤ g x for every g in G and every x). Then for every d and n, the state at step n of the run started at d that, at each step, passes the amount through all the maps of G in order is at least d.

author: claude
text: Let G be a list of maps on natural numbers, none of which lowers its argument (x ≤ g x for every g in G and every x). Then for every d and n, the state at step n of the run started by an operator at d that, at each step, passes the amount through all the maps of G in order is at least d.

author: claude
text: Let ρ be a rule whose output at step t depends only on record entries at steps s with s + ℓ < t, and let 0 < a. If, for every record δ whose entries' components differ by at most d, the amount from x₀ changed each step by ρ's and δ's additions and removals stays between a and b, then a + (ℓ + 1)(d + d) ≤ b.

author: claude
text: Let ρ be a rule whose output at step t depends only on record entries at steps s with s + ℓ < t, and let 0 < a. If, for every record δ of disturbances from the environment whose entries' components differ by at most d, the amount from x₀ changed each step by ρ's and δ's additions and removals stays between a and b, then a + (ℓ + 1)(d + d) ≤ b.

author: claude
text: For a web W and level histories l, l' and l'': if l includes l' in W and l' includes l'' in W, then l includes l'' in W, where l includes l' when, at every step t and for every f, whenever W admits f under l' at t it also admits f under l at t.

author: claude
text: For a web W and level histories l, l' and l'': if l includes l' in W and l' includes l'' in W, then l includes l'' in W, where l includes l' when, at every step t and for every f, whenever an observer finds that W admits f under l' at t it also admits f under l at t.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a predicate S over positions, steps and forms, a position p, and level histories l, l', l'': if l retains l' (every form satisfying S at p that W admits at a step under l' it also admits under l) and l' retains l'', then l retains l''.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a predicate S over positions, steps and forms, a position p, and level histories l, l', l'' of one keeper: if l retains l' (every form satisfying S at p that W admits at a step under l' it also admits under l) and l' retains l'', then l retains l''.

author: claude
text: For whole numbers p, q, n, h, N, g with (p+q)h + g = Np: the total, over all true/false sequences of length n whose count of trues times N is at most h times n, of each sequence's weight from p and q, multiplied by n squared times g squared, is at most N squared times n times pq(p+q) to the power n.

author: claude
text: For whole numbers p, q, n, h, N, g with (p+q)h + g = Np: the total, over all true/false sequences of length n in the population whose count of trues times N is at most h times n, of each sequence's weight from p and q, multiplied by n squared times g squared, is at most N squared times n times pq(p+q) to the power n.

author: claude
text: For a flow L balancing a web W, an amount m, a step T, a condition c and a count n: if at each of n steps from T the net change at c stays within c's distance from m and opposes it (net taking when above m, net giving when below), then c's distance from m after those steps is at most its distance at T minus n.

author: claude
text: For a flow L balancing a web W, an amount m, a step T, a condition c and a count n: if at each of n steps from T the net change at c stays within c's distance from m and opposes it (net taking when above m, net giving from the surroundings when below), then c's distance from m after those steps is at most its distance at T minus n.

author: claude
text: Let K be a class of relations between Boolean predicates on X containing, for each weighting positive on the list L, the relation ranking b below a when b's weighted total over L is less than a's, with every member R having R b a whenever a widens b on L. Then a widens b on L if and only if R b a for every R in K.

author: claude
text: Let K be a class of relations between Boolean predicates on X containing, for each weighting positive on the list L, the relation ranking b below a when b's weighted total over L is less than a's, with every member R having R b a whenever a widens b on L. Then a widens b on L, within its environment, if and only if R b a for every R in K.

author: claude
text: Let P be a process and γ mark some labels, with p holding before every unmarked step after which it holds. If a trace along label list l leads from s to t with p at t, then p holds at s, or l splits as u, a marked label a, v, with u leading from s to m, a from m to m' where p holds, and v from m' to t.

author: claude
text: Let P be a process and γ mark some labels, with p holding before every unmarked step after which it holds. If a trace along label list l leads from s to t with p at t, then p holds at s, or, as the truth of p must enter somewhere, l splits as u, a marked label a, v, with u leading from s to m, a from m to m' where p holds, and v from m' to t.

author: claude
text: For a map n on states and a state s: s returns under n if and only if there is a positive number p such that applying n to s p times gives back s.

author: claude
text: For a map n on states and a state s: s returns under n if and only if there is in truth a positive number p such that applying n to s p times gives back s.

author: claude
text: For natural numbers p, q, k, n, u and v with v ≤ u: the total, over all Boolean sequences of length n with at least k trues, of p to the number of trues times q to the number of falses, multiplied by u^k · v^n, is at most (p·u + q·v)^n · v^k.

author: claude
text: For natural numbers p, q, k, n, u and v with v ≤ u: the total, over all Boolean sequences of length n with at least k trues, of p to the number of trues times q to the number of falses, multiplied by u^k · v^n, is at most (p·u + q·v)^n · v^k, a bound set by the law of large numbers.

author: claude
text: If, for every process and every property K of its runs, K being verifiable (every run with K has a finite stretch every run sharing which has K) makes not-K refutable (every run where not-K fails has such a stretch every run sharing which has not-K fail), then every Boolean sequence that is not all false has a true term.

author: claude
text: If, for every process and every property K of its runs, K being verifiable by an observer (every run with K has a finite stretch every run sharing which has K) makes not-K refutable (every run where not-K fails has such a stretch every run sharing which has not-K fail), then every Boolean sequence that is not all false has a true term.

author: claude
text: Let G be a list of maps on natural numbers. If the state at step n of the run started at d that, at each step, passes the amount through all the maps of G in order is less than d, then some map in G lowers some argument: there are g in G and x with g x < x.

author: claude
text: Let G be a list of maps on natural numbers. If the state at step n of the run started by a controller at d that, at each step, passes the amount through all the maps of G in order is less than d, then some map in G lowers some argument: there are g in G and x with g x < x.

author: claude
text: Under the successor map on natural numbers, 0 is drawn (there is an absorbing set into which the successor draws 0), and the successor map is lossless.

author: claude
text: Under the successor map on natural numbers, 0 is drawn (there is an absorbing set into which the successor draws 0 from its surroundings), and the successor map is lossless.

author: claude
text: For a map n on states, a state s all of whose iterates lie in a finite list l, and a map g from states to outcomes with decidable equality: it is not the case that no step T exists after which, at every step t, elimination over lasso-shaped candidates applied to the first t outcomes of the orbit returns exactly the outcome at t.

author: claude
text: For a map n on states, a state s all of whose iterates lie in a finite list l, and a map g from states to outcomes with decidable equality: it is not the case that no step T exists after which, at every step t, elimination over lasso-shaped candidates applied to knowledge of the first t outcomes of the orbit returns exactly the outcome at t.

author: claude
text: For a sequence g of states and a sequence m of labels: the process whose steps are exactly the transitions g and m show (from g at n with label m at n to g at n+1) is deterministic if and only if, whenever two indices have the same state and the same label, their next states are equal.

author: claude
text: For a sequence g of states and a sequence m of labels: the process whose steps are exactly the transitions g and m show (from g at n with label m at n to g at n+1) is deterministic if and only if, whenever two indices have the same state and the same label in the same environment, their next states are equal.

author: claude
text: For natural numbers p, q and n: p + q times the total, over all Boolean sequences of length n, of each sequence's weight (p to the number of trues times q to the number of falses) times its number of trues equals n · p · (p + q)^n.

author: claude
text: For natural numbers p, q and n: p + q times the total, over all Boolean sequences of length n that a sampler might draw, of each sequence's weight (p to the number of trues times q to the number of falses) times its number of trues equals n · p · (p + q)^n.

author: claude
text: Let r assign an amount to each element at each step so that, while an element is unsupported in W, its amount never increases, strictly decreases when the element is active, and strictly decreases when positive. If f is unsupported at every step from S on and r at S for f is at most n, then f is not active in W at step S + n.

author: claude
text: Let r assign an amount to each element at each step so that, while an element is unsupported in W, its amount never increases, strictly decreases when the element is active, and strictly decreases when positive. If f is unsupported by its environment at every step from S on and r at S for f is at most n, then f is not active in W at step S + n.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a relation r, a predicate σ and an element f, the own part at f of W's valuation built from r and σ contains (f, t) for every step t; the elements g with (g, t) in it for every t form a region closed under r containing f; and every region closed under r containing f contains the first component of every pair in it.

author: claude
text: For a web W, a relation r, a predicate σ and an element f, the own part at f of W's valuation built from r and σ contains (f, t) for every step t; the elements g with (g, t) in it for every t form, by nature, a region closed under r containing f; and every region closed under r containing f contains the first component of every pair in it.

author: claude
text: If a predicate P on I holds for every i, then for any predicate B on I, P holds for every i that satisfies B.

author: claude
text: Let V be a web and π a passing relation such that whatever is active at step t + 1 was active at t or is passed to by some element active at t. If a arises at t (inactive at t, active at t + 1), then some b active at t passes to a at t.

author: claude
text: Let V be a web and π a passing relation such that whatever is active at step t + 1 was active at t or is passed to by some element active at t. If a arises at t (inactive at t, active at t + 1), then some sender b active at t passes to a at t.

author: claude
text: Let f be a map on a type S, and let the list a contain every element of S. Then f is lossless if and only if every element x returns under f.

text: Let f be a map on a type S, and let the list a contain every element of S. Then f is lossless if and only if, as an observer following f would find, every element x returns under f.

author: claude
text: In a web W, for level histories l and l': if l widens on l' (l includes l' and exceeds it), then l and l' are not mixed (it is not the case that each exceeds the other).

author: claude
text: In a web W, for level histories l and l' that a manager compares: if l widens on l' (l includes l' and exceeds it), then l and l' are not mixed (it is not the case that each exceeds the other).

author: claude
text: For a list P and a weight w assigning a natural number to each member: the square of the total weight of P equals the length of P times the total of the squared weights if and only if w gives every two members of P the same value.

author: claude
text: For a list P and a weight w assigning a natural number to each member: the square of the total weight of P equals the length of P times the total of the squared weights, by the law of averages, if and only if w gives every two members of P the same value.

author: claude
text: For a predicate q on items and a list of items: some number counts the items of the list satisfying q if and only if, for every item in the list, q either holds or fails.

author: claude
text: For a predicate q on items and a list of items from a wider pool: some number counts the items of the list satisfying q if and only if, for every item in the list, q either holds or fails.

author: claude
text: For an element f, a predicate σ and a position p: some region containing f (every region being closed under the empty relation) has σ p t g for every step t and every member g if and only if σ p t f holds for every step t.

author: claude
text: For an element f, a predicate σ and a position p: some region containing f (every region being closed under the empty relation), chosen by an evaluator, has σ p t g for every step t and every member g if and only if σ p t f holds for every step t.

author: claude
text: For a relation R on items, an item f, a predicate S on positions, times and items, and a position p: some region that contains f and is closed under R has S holding at p at every time for every item in it if and only if S holds of p, t and g for every time t and every item g in every R-closed region containing f.

author: claude
text: For a relation R on items, an item f, a predicate S on positions, times and items, and a position p: some region that contains f and is closed under R by its nature has S holding at p at every time for every item in it if and only if S holds of p, t and g for every time t and every item g in every R-closed region containing f.

author: claude
text: For generations of items in which each member's amount is its number of offspring, and a step t at which every child's amount at t+1 equals its parent's amount at t: the square of the size at t+1 is less than the size at t times the size at t+2 if and only if the concordance at t of offspring number with amount is positive.

author: claude
text: For generations of items in which each member's amount is its number of offspring in the habitat, and a step t at which every child's amount at t+1 equals its parent's amount at t: the square of the size at t+1 is less than the size at t times the size at t+2 if and only if the concordance at t of offspring number with amount is positive.

author: claude
text: For a predicate p on items and steps, listed exactly and without repetition at each step by l, a step S and a count n: the number listed at S+n plus the number of items ceasing to satisfy p over the n steps from S equals the number listed at S plus the number coming to satisfy p over those steps.

author: claude
text: For a predicate p on items and steps, listed exactly and without repetition at each step by l, a step S and a count n: the number listed at S+n plus the number of items ceasing to satisfy p over the n steps from S equals the number listed at S plus the number coming in from the environment to satisfy p over those steps.

author: claude
text: Let f be a map on a type S with decidable equality, and let the list a contain every element of S. Then f is lossless if and only if no element x is drawn under f, that is, for no x is there an absorbing set into which f draws x.

author: claude
text: Let f be a map on a type S with decidable equality, and let the list a contain every element of S. Then f is lossless if and only if no element x is drawn under f, that is, for no x is there an absorbing set, shared with the rest of the system, into which f draws x.

author: claude
text: For an update on sets of elements that preserves inclusion, a step n and an element a: a belongs to the set reached after n updates from every starting set if and only if it belongs to the set reached after n updates from the empty set.

author: claude
text: For an update on sets of elements that preserves inclusion, a step n and an element a: a belongs to the set reached after n updates from every starting set a designer might pick if and only if it belongs to the set reached after n updates from the empty set.

author: claude
text: For relations R and A on items: closure under R-or-A relates exactly the same pairs as closure under R alone if and only if, for every pair g, h related by A, h lies in every R-closed region containing g.

author: claude
text: For relations R and A on items: closure under R-or-A relates exactly the same pairs as closure under R alone in the existing order if and only if, for every pair g, h related by A, h lies in every R-closed region containing g.

author: claude
text: For an item f, a predicate S over positions, times and items, and a position p: some region containing f and closed under the relation holding between every two items has S holding at p at every time for every item in it if and only if S holds of p, t and g for every time t and every item g.

author: claude
text: For an item f, a predicate S over positions, times and items, and a position p someone takes: some region containing f and closed under the relation holding between every two items has S holding at p at every time for every item in it if and only if S holds of p, t and g for every time t and every item g.

author: claude
